text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri opens dialogue with Maronite patriarch Sfeir over the decision to shut down religious radio and television stations.
-The General Labour Confederation (CGTL) calls for a sit-in on Wednesday in front of the ministerial palace to protest a law slashing the number of private television and radio stations in Lebanon.
-Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said that the Arab-Israeli peace process is in danger.
-Central bank first deputy chief Saidi says the financial situation in Lebanon is under control.

-A "hot week" awaits the government over the audiovisual media law. Protests at the Maronite patriarchate, and patriarch Sfeir says he is against bias in dealing with the television and radio stations.
-Weekend Israeli air raid on Hizbollah targets in south Lebanon hills after guerrilla attack on Israeli-backed militiamen.
-Minister of displaced people Jumblatt urges the government to speed up the return of villagers displaced in the civil war to their original homes "to erase the scars of war".
-Roman Catholic schools in Lebanon to hold a strike on October 17 to protest the closure of religious television and radio stations.
-Chairman of Middle East Airlines (MEA) Salam says Israeli blitz against Lebanon in April caused the airline to suffer a loss of $15 million.
